The `uniqueSorted` utility function does not guard against non-array inputs. If `values` is null, undefined, or not an array, calling `values.filter` will throw a `TypeError`.

To align with the general rules for robust utility functions, please ensure it safely defaults to an empty array when the input is not an array.

```suggestion
function uniqueSorted(values) {
  const arr = Array.isArray(values) ? values : [];
  return [...new Set(arr.filter((value) => value !== null && value !== undefined && value !== ''))]
    .map(String)
    .sort(compareByteOrder);
}
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. Ensure utility functions (such as sorting, filtering, or mapping helpers) are robust against non-array inputs by returning a safe default (e.g., an empty array) to fail closed gracefully instead of throwing a TypeError.
</details>

Fixed in `e1c5fabed96ad9d32fcc9d8d74db05dac96024a3`: individual `row.raw_candidates` entries now get shape validation, malformed/null entries and missing stable IDs emit critical diagnostics, and malformed candidates classify as `blocked_quarantined` with no promotion/runtime/review-task acceptance path.

Fixed in `e1c5fabed96ad9d32fcc9d8d74db05dac96024a3`: `buildSemanticKgFullCandidateClassification` now normalizes null/non-object options to `{}` and only merges path overrides when `opts.paths` is an object. Regression covers `buildSemanticKgFullCandidateClassification(null)` no-throw with default pass counts.
